strengths: Novel structural approach using uniform spanning trees for principled sequence randomization in AR models, balancing flexibility with spatial coherence
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 1-2) explaining the core contribution
Comprehensive experimental methodology including multiple baselines, ablation studies (Tables 2-3), and detailed hyperparameter configurations
Well-designed evaluation protocol with multiple metrics (FID, IS, Precision, Recall) and fair model capacity comparisons
Addresses a genuine limitation of conventional AR models' inability to flexibly change inference sequence orders
Reproducible work with mentioned code availability and complete experimental details
weaknesses: Marginal empirical improvements: STAR-XXL achieves 338.8 FID tied with RandAR-XXL baseline (Table 1), with most variants showing only minor gains that do not justify added complexity
Weak theoretical justification: lacks rigorous analysis for why spanning trees specifically are superior; claims about 'maintaining prior knowledge' remain intuitive rather than proven
Unconvincing downstream task evaluation: image inpainting results (Figure 6, Table 2) are mixed and inconsistent, with modest improvements that do not demonstrate clear practical utility
Missing computational overhead analysis: no quantification of costs from spanning tree sampling and BFS traversal, critical given marginal empirical gains
Narrow experimental scope: only ImageNet-1k at 256×256 tested; no evaluation on other datasets or higher resolutions; limited to FID/IS metrics without perceptual metrics or human evaluation
Disconnected conditional entropy analysis: Figures 3-4 analyze prediction entropy patterns but fail to establish clear connection to visual generation quality
Ad-hoc design choices: random masking strategy for inpainting (Appendix B) lacks principled justification and appears orthogonal to the spanning tree contribution
Limited downstream task diversity: only image inpainting tested; broader evaluation on super-resolution, editing, or other applications needed to support flexibility claims
No failure case analysis or discussion of when spanning trees underperform, limiting insights into method applicability

strengths: Well-motivated sequence order strategy using spanning trees that elegantly balances spatial structure and flexibility, with clear articulation of why this middle ground is superior to both fixed orders and random permutations

Comprehensive experimental evaluation including extensive ablation studies (locality effects, center bias, conditional entropy analysis, DFS/BFS comparison) that provide good insights into design choices
Practical architectural simplicity requiring only minimal modifications to standard decoder-only Transformers, making the method easily adoptable by practitioners
Competitive empirical results on ImageNet-1k image generation with STAR-XXL achieving FID scores comparable to or better than several baseline methods
Thorough presentation with clear motivation, well-organized methodology, effective visualizations, and detailed implementation details in supplementary material
Solid theoretical grounding in entropy analysis and intuitive explanations for why spanning tree properties preserve prior knowledge while enabling flexibility
weaknesses: Significantly limited experimental scope: evaluation only on ImageNet-1k at single resolution (256×256) with no experiments on other benchmarks (COCO, CelebA-HQ, LSUN) or higher resolutions (512×512+) standard in recent visual generation work

Incremental contribution: the core innovation is a token sequencing strategy rather than a new architecture, loss function, or fundamental modeling approach—essentially a better way to order existing tokens

Incomplete theoretical justification: entropy convergence conjecture (Section 3.2) stated but not rigorously proven; connection between spanning tree properties and claimed performance improvements lacks formal analysis

Unfair baseline comparisons in Table 1 with varying model sizes (261M–804M parameters) and unclear if all methods trained identically, making it difficult to isolate the sequence order strategy's contribution
Mixed empirical results in key settings: Figure 7 shows RAR outperforming STAR on inpainting at lower masking ratios (0.1–0.3); Table 2 shows performance gaps unexplained by authors

Computational overhead not thoroughly analyzed: Table 4 mentions 0.56 ms per instance for spanning tree sampling without context; missing total inference time comparisons and training cost analysis of handling multiple sequence orders

Postfix completion mechanism has acknowledged limitation: Appendix A admits violations of core masking assumptions are common in practice, contradicting claimed theoretical validity and requiring ad-hoc multi-turn inference solutions
Missing analysis of failure modes, design trade-offs, and clear guidance for practitioners on when to use STAR versus alternatives
Representation learning analysis (Section 5, Figure 9) feels tangential to main contribution and appears disconnected from core narrative
No explicit discussion of method limitations or broader societal impact, which are expected in modern venue submissions
